c.tagline: Medieval canal city of cobblestones, chocolate shops, and Flemish Primitive art.

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis are metered with fixed start-up and per-km rates set by the city; ranks are at the Markt, the train station, and major hotels.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number and connects to police, fire, and ambulance.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Pickpockets work the dense day-trip crowds around the Markt and Belfry in high season.

hood_desc: The postcard core of Bruges around the Markt, Belfry, and Burg square, packed with museums, chocolate shops, and canal-boat docks; best for first-timers who want everything within walking distance, though it's also the most crowded with day-trippers.
A quieter, more residential quarter east of the centre around the Jerusalem Church and the Lace Centre; good for travelers wanting an authentic feel a short walk from the sights.
A laid-back local neighborhood northwest of the centre with independent cafes and the Sint-Gilliskerk; suited to travelers wanting a residential, non-touristy base.
The area around Bruges railway station, with easy access to trains and buses; practical for budget travelers and those arriving late or leaving early.
A green, largely residential suburb south of the centre near Beisbroek Park and the Tillegembos woods; suited to families and nature-minded travelers wanting space and quiet.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink across Belgium.

transit.hours: Buses generally run from about 6:00 AM to midnight; Bruges has no metro or tram.
transit.pay: Contactless bank card or the De Lijn app are standard; single tickets can also be bought from the driver at a surcharge.
transit.note: Bruges has no metro or tram; De Lijn buses radiate from the train station and Markt, but the compact historic centre is easily explored on foot or by bike.

train: Brugge railway station (NMBS/SNCB intercity trains to Brussels, Ghent, Ostend)
ferry: P&O Ferries/DFDS via nearby Zeebrugge (UK connections)

transit.m: Direct train Brussels Airport to Bruges (~70 min, hourly)

tip.r: Service is usually included in the bill; rounding up or leaving small change (5-10%) for good service is appreciated but not expected.

places.name: Chez Vincent

places.name: Restaurant Diligence

food.name: Stoofvlees
food.desc: Flemish beef stew, or carbonade flamande, braised for hours in dark abbey beer with mustard and a slice of bread; sweet, dark and served with frites.

places.name: Bij Koen & Marijke

places.name: 't Hof van Beroep

places.name: Restaurant Diligence

food.name: Waterzooi
food.desc: Creamy Flemish stew of chicken or fish with leek, carrot and potato bound in egg yolk and cream; a gentle antidote to a cold canal walk.

places.name: Bij Koen & Marijke

places.name: Park Restaurant
places.note: Comfortable brasserie by the park with Belgian standards on the menu.

food.name: Garnaalkroketten
food.desc: Crisp-fried croquettes filled with a bechamel thick with tiny grey North Sea shrimp, served with fried parsley and a lemon wedge.

places.name: 't Hof van Beroep

food.name: Belgian waffles
food.desc: Two kinds: the dense, caramelised Liege waffle eaten in the hand, and the lighter rectangular Brussels waffle dusted with icing sugar.

places.note: Hatch-window Liege waffles between the Markt and the Burg; near-permanent queue.

places.name: House of Waffles
places.note: Sit-down waffle house with both styles and a long list of toppings.

places.name: Lizzie's Wafels

food.name: Speculoos and Bruges chocolate
food.desc: Spiced caramelised biscuits stamped in wooden moulds, and hand-made pralines from a city with more chocolatiers per street than almost anywhere.

places.name: The Chocolate Line
places.note: Dominique Persoone's experimental praline shop, Bruges' best-known chocolatier.

places.name: Dumon Chocolatier
places.note: Family chocolatier with small batches sold from a tiny historic shopfront.

places.name: Sukerbuyc
places.note: Old-fashioned chocolate shop and tearoom good for speculoos with coffee.

food.name: Belgian beer
food.desc: Trappist and abbey ales, sour lambics and the local Brugse Zot brewed inside the city walls; served in its own branded glass.

places.name: Brouwerij De Halve Maan
places.note: City-centre brewery of Brugse Zot with tours and a courtyard tasting cafe.

places.name: 't Brugs Beertje
places.note: Legendary beer cafe with hundreds of Belgian bottles and knowledgeable staff.

places.name: Staminee De Garre
places.note: Hidden alley tavern pouring its own 11 percent tripel with a cube of cheese.

food.name: Jenever
food.desc: Juniper-based Low Countries spirit poured to the brim in a tulip glass; drunk neat and cold, plain or in fruit and spice flavours.

places.name: Cafe Vlissinghe

places.name: 't Poatersgat

places.name: Cafe Rose Red

landmarks: Belfry of Bruges (Belfort)
Climb 366 spiraling steps up the iconic 83-meter medieval bell tower on the Markt for carillon concerts and rooftop views over gabled Flanders.
Markt Square
Bruges' bustling main square is ringed by step-gabled guildhalls, horse-drawn carriages and the neo-Gothic Provincial Court beneath the mighty Belfry.
Rozenhoedkaai and the Canals
The Quay of the Rosary is Belgium's most photographed corner, where canal boats drift past medieval brick facades mirrored in still green water.
Basilica of the Holy Blood
On Burg square, this double chapel guards a venerated relic of Christ's blood brought from the Crusades, paraded annually in the UNESCO-listed Holy Blood Procession.
Church of Our Lady
Its 115-meter brick tower, among the world's tallest, shelters Michelangelo's Madonna and Child, the only sculpture to leave Italy in his lifetime.
Begijnhof (Beguinage)
A serene white-walled courtyard of poplars and daffodils, founded in 1245 for lay religious women and now home to Benedictine sisters.
Minnewater (Lake of Love)
Swans glide across this romantic poplar-lined lake at the city's southern edge, where legend promises eternal love to couples crossing its bridge.
Groeningemuseum
The definitive collection of Flemish Primitives, from Jan van Eyck's jewel-like panels to Bosch and Memling, chronicles six centuries of Low Countries art.
Sint-Janshospitaal (Old St. John's Hospital)
One of Europe's oldest hospital buildings, an 800-year-old ward complex, displays Hans Memling's exquisite shrine paintings amid medieval medical history.
De Halve Maan Brewery
Bruges' last family brewery in the city center offers rooftop-view tours and famously pipes its Brugse Zot beer through a three-kilometer underground pipeline.

train.note: No international trains call at Bruges - for Eurostar you change at Brussels-Midi, about an hour away. Domestic trains run to Brussels every half hour, Ghent in 25 minutes and Ostend in 15. The station is a 15-minute walk south of the Markt. Belgian fares are fixed-price, so there is no advantage in booking early.

bus.note: Coaches stop at the station. FlixBus runs to Brussels, Amsterdam, Paris and London; the UK route includes a full immigration check at the Channel, so carry your passport. De Lijn's coastal tram from nearby Ostend is one of the longest tram lines in the world and runs the length of the Belgian coast.

intl.to: Hull (UK) - sails from Zeebrugge, ~20 min by train from Bruges, overnight

ferry.note: Bruges itself has only canal sightseeing boats, but Zeebrugge - 20 minutes away by train - is a real international port with P&O's overnight sailing to Hull, which carries cars and foot passengers. The Rotterdam and Dunkirk alternatives are also within easy reach. Book cabins ahead in summer; the crossing takes about 13 hours.

half.name: Ghent
half.blurb: Medieval university city of canals, a fortified castle and Gothic guild houses, quieter and less touristed than Bruges.

half.name: Brussels
half.blurb: Belgian capital with the Grand Place, EU institutions and Art Nouveau architecture, about an hour by train.

half.name: Ypres
half.blurb: WWI battlefield town with the In Flanders Fields museum and the nightly Last Post ceremony at the Menin Gate.

half.name: Antwerp
half.blurb: Fashion and diamond-trading city with a Gothic cathedral and one of Europe's grandest train stations.
